newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks reverse day's losses to end higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks reverse day's losses to end higher.

text.p: French shares found external support from Wall Street's push upwards and reversed the day's retreat to end higher, traders said.
Market operators noted non-domestic buying, particularly from U.S. funds. Prior to the entry of Wall Street bulls, Paris equities were down on profit-taking on strong strong gains.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 9.99 points or 0.46 percent at 2,161.54 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,168 from 2,157.5 on Monday's close.

* Promodes closed up 19 francs at 1,420. Dupont Denant raised its recommendation on the retailer to outperform from performance in line. The brokerage expects a strong rebound of the order of 30 percent in Promodes' 1997 results

* Cie Generale des Eaux finished up eight francs at 586. Merrill Lynch upped the stock to accumulate from neutral, citing the "profit dilution" - exceptional gain - for 1997 from its Cegetel telecommunications subsidiary, which will offset its property problems
* Bouygues firmed 9.40 francs at 485. The building company posted H1 net attributable loss 146 million francs
* Bouygues forecast the 1996 result would be close to the 1994 out-turn thanks mainly to capital gains from asset sales
* The government denied it had any plans to strip part of the mining assets of nickle producer Eramet in New Caledonia, as part of talks over mining reserves in the Pacific territory
* The stock closed up 11.80 francs at 277.80 after the news lifted the stock of a year low hit on Tuesday morning
* Eurotunnel closed down 0.80 francs at 8.35, amid disappointment over the debt/equity conversion price of 10.40 fr/share for the banks which will get 45.5 percent of capital.
